channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Azadi Tower: Architect Watches From Exile As Beloved Iranian Landmark Coopted By Regime
item.description: Soon after his most famous public monument was completed, Hossein Amanat was forced to flee Iran amid the Islamic revolution. The architect spoke to RFE/RL about watching his Azadi Tower being used as a backdrop for Islamic regime military parades.

item.title: Diplomacy Or Conflict? US-Iran Crisis Now '50-50,' Experts Say
item.description: After US-Iran nuclear talks in Geneva ended without a breakthrough, experts say the crisis is at a tipping point as military buildups continue and both sides remain “very far apart.”

item.title: Will EU Sanctions On Russia Stall As Hungary And Slovakia Leverage Oil Vetoes?
item.description: As the European Union races to approve its new sanctions package on Russia by the fourth anniversary of Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine next week, a new obstacle may have appeared.

item.title: Iran, Russia Hold Naval Drills Amid US Military Build Up In Arabian Sea
item.description: Iran and Russia launched joint naval drills in Iran’s southern waters on February 19, as the United States continues expanding its military presence in the Arabian Sea.

item.title: Russia, Iran Hold Joint Naval Drills As US Renews Threats Of Military Action
item.description: The Iranian and Russian navies have been conducting joint drills in the Sea of Oman and the northern Indian Ocean as the United States issued new threats against Tehran.

item.title: Ukraine Peace Talks Are Stalling. A Firebrand Russian Historian May Be To Blame.
item.description: Why did Ukraine’s president refer to the latest round of peace talks using a barnyard epithet? The presence of a firebrand, revisionist Russian historian-- whose writings have been derided as propaganda – as part of the Russian delegation is why.

item.title: Central Asia's 'Water Tower' Is Drying Up As Glaciers Vanish
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Lake Issyk-Kul has been shrinking at an alarming rate over the past decade, receding by up to 10 meters in some places, according to research. One of the world's largest alpine lakes is threatened by climate change, drought, and melting glaciers.

item.title: Belarusian Former Presidential Candidate Mikalay Statkevich Freed From Prison After Stroke
item.description: Belarusian former presidential candidate Mikalay Statkevich, who has been imprisoned for over ten years, was released to his home in Minsk after having a stroke in jail, according to his family.

item.title: On Icy Baltic Coast, NATO Forces Rehearse For War And Hybrid Threats
item.description: Some 10,000 troops from 13 countries are participating in NATO military exercises on Germany's Baltic coast. NATO officials said the exercises show the alliance's ability to respond to hybrid warfare and conventional threats, along with the cutting-edge drone technology seen in the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Four Years Of The Ukraine Invasion: Has Russia’s Military Learned To Fight A Better War?
item.description: Four years of war against Ukraine means four years of learning for Russia’s armed forces. But how much have they actually learned, how much have they actually reformed, and how worried should people be once the Ukraine war does end?
